cohort: The study participants included 4,439,778 pregnant women who gave birth in Korea between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2016, divided into Korean and immigrant women groups.
finding: Immigrant women in Korea had higher odds of gestational diabetes mellitus (aOR: 1.24) and cesarean section (aOR: 1.26), but lower odds of preeclampsia (aOR: 0.84) and postpartum hemorrhage (aOR: 0.96) compared to Korean women.
mod_finding: The odds of cesarean section were higher in immigrant women than in Korean women (adjusted OR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.25-1.28).
followup_time: Outcomes were assessed during pregnancy and postpartum, with no specific follow-up duration after birth mentioned beyond the postpartum period.
